inputs.root_cause: IPYNB-LIFECYCLE-001's 6 obligations shared one 3-test citation proving strict/tolerant modes well but leaving the other five clauses (save, load, validate-as-callable, deterministic serialization, detected-vs-declared version) generically or thinly cited. This mirrors ORA-LIFECYCLE-001's earlier tick almost exactly (same six standard clauses every format in this codebase carries), but investigating load/save individually surfaced a genuine, narrow test gap this ora tick did not have: stream-object support (Source/Destination types both accept anything with read()/write(), and the reader explicitly branches on hasattr(source, 'read')) had zero test coverage anywhere in the shipped ipynb namespace, confirmed by first checking (and correctly rejecting) the deprecated shadow-package test file that does exercise similar-looking load paths but does not count as shipped-namespace evidence.

execution_steps: 1. Pulled all 6 IPYNB-LIFECYCLE-001 rule_texts, recognized the standard load/save/validate/deterministic/strict-tolerant/version cluster shape already closed for ORA-LIFECYCLE-001 earlier this session, and began mapping each clause to its specific shipped-namespace test.

2. Searched broadly for load-from-path/stream/bytes, validate-as-callable, and detected/declared-version tests across the whole ipynb test suite (not just the obligation-named files) and found two candidate hits in test_ipynb_codec.py -- checked its imports first and found it imports from the bare `ipynb.*` package, the deprecated shadow package this codebase's own test docstrings (GAP-017/GAP-018) explicitly bar from counting as shipped-namespace coverage. Excluded it and continued searching.

3. Grepped specifically for BytesIO/StringIO/stream usage across every test_obligation_*.py file and test_production_namespace.py: zero hits. Checked reader.py/writer.py's actual Source/Destination type aliases and _read_source's implementation directly -- confirmed stream objects (anything with a str-returning read()) are explicitly supported in source (hasattr(source, 'read') branch), so this is a genuine test-coverage gap, not an unbuilt feature.

4. Closed the gap with 2 new tests in test_production_namespace.py: test_load_from_a_readable_text_stream (io.StringIO as load() source) and test_dump_writes_to_a_writable_text_stream (io.StringIO as dump() destination, reloaded to confirm round-trip). Ran both directly before citing: passed on the first attempt, confirming the source path already worked correctly.

5. Found precise existing tests for the remaining four clauses: deterministic serialization (test_repeated_writes_are_byte_identical, test_roundtrip_is_stable_across_two_passes, both parametrized across every indent setting); validate-as-callable (test_schema_diagnostics_expose_stable_codes_and_precise_paths, a stronger, more specific citation than the previously-used generic one); detected-vs-declared version (a document with declared_version.minor is None still resolving a separate concrete detected_version, proven not to silently rewrite the declared field even after a recovery pass that synthesizes several other missing values).

6. Applied all 6 evidence edits via the same obligation_id-delimited text-block script pattern used across nine prior ora/ipynb ticks, extracting the actual proof_requirements boilerplate from an untouched sibling programmatically. Ran the reconciler: clean pass, no errors, first attempt. Ran the full ipynb suite: 690 passed (688 baseline + 2 new), 0 regressions.

evidence.oracle: none -- this is format_factory's own self-consistent test evidence, not independently cross-checked against nbformat or Jupyter itself for these specific lifecycle behaviors. Labeled SELF-CONSISTENT per the FF6 execution-recovery directive's GAP-008 rule, not VERIFIED.
evidence.why_all_6_moved_and_one_real_gap_closed: All six clauses were either already proven by existing tests (needing only precise re-citation) or, for load/save, proven correct once a genuinely missing test (stream-object support) was added. Unlike several ora clusters this session, no clause here required staying at partial with an honestly-named unbuilt gap -- the underlying source was already complete, just under-tested for one input shape.
